_comment: Signal's tool registry, read by the setup CLI (tools/setup) and the setup skill (.claude/skills/setup). Paths are relative to the repo root, where every command runs. {email} is the address the user gave in an 'email' step; {port} is the console's port (setup --port, default 8790). Step kinds: run (a command), copy (an example config, kept if it already exists), manual (instructions the user follows), confirm (a yes/no choice), email (asks an address and writes it into source constants), env (asks a non-secret value for .env), settings (creates the tool's config files from their examples and asks its settings, from data/settings/<tool>.json; done only when no placeholder is left; 'group' picks an optional group such as the assignment checker), samples (copytone writing samples). 'terminal' steps need the user's own interactive terminal, so the agent never runs them. 'opens_browser' steps open the user's browser to sign in, so someone must be there. 'Automatic' steps (required run and copy steps that are neither terminal nor opens_browser) are the ones `setup auto` runs unasked; optional steps always wait for their own click. 'group' (Core, Everyday, Hardware, Extras) and 'cost' (a few words: time, account, hardware) are how the setup window's Pick page lists a tool. A step's mcp/permissions apply only once that step is done; a tool's apply once all its required steps are done. 'verify' is a cheap read-only check: exit 0 passes, and its last stdout line may be one JSON object {words, fix, command} (tools/setup/README.md, Verify checks). 'fix' is the sentence a failed check shows when it gives none. 'evidence' lists local, gitignored paths only a machine where the tool was set up has (its venv; the job runner's run-log folder): a tool setup has no record of reads as set up only when they all exist, its servers and hooks are in Claude Code's config and its verify check passes (tools/setup/README.md, Found already set up). A tool with no 'evidence' is never found that way, and a path checked into the repo must never be listed (a fresh clone has it). 'consent' is one plain line for the consent page (setup plan, before the exact entries): what Claude may do without asking once the tool is added, shown once a granting part is done (its rules or hooks, or a done 'unattended_claude' step). Every tool with permissions, hooks or an 'unattended_claude' step has one. 'unattended_claude' marks a step that registers a scheduled Claude run with tools, which acts with nobody asked.

tools.name: Agent rules (AGENTS.md)
tools.description: The rules every agent follows in this repo. Its one setting is when an agent stops and hands off to a fresh one as its context fills up.

steps.title: Choose when agents hand off (context threshold)

tools.name: Catch-up brief for when you're away
tools.description: Sessions log what you should hear about; 'brief me' gives a ranked catch-up, and while you're Away, sessions keep working without you.
tools.consent: Claude can log to the brief, read it, mark items handled and turn Away on or off without asking each time. A hook adds the brief and the away rules to your prompts, reads the session's transcript, and marks items seen once Claude has passed them on.

steps.title: Install

tools.fix: Set the brief up again with setup brief.

tools.name: Usage tracker
tools.description: Keeps your 5-hour and weekly Claude usage and the running subagent count in one file, for the status line and the console.
tools.consent: Claude gets nothing new to do. A hook counts subagents as they start and stop.

steps.title: Install
Show usage in Claude Code's status line (writes statusLine in your user settings, ~/.claude/settings.json)

tools.fix: Set the usage tracker up again with setup usage.

tools.name: Context meter
tools.description: Tells every agent, subagents included, how full its context window is, and to hand off at the AGENTS.md threshold.
tools.consent: Claude gets nothing new to do. After each tool call a hook checks how full its context is, and tells it when the level changes.

steps.title: Install
Create tools/contextmeter/contextmeter.toml and set your context window size (200k or 1M)

tools.fix: Set the context meter up again with setup contextmeter.

tools.name: Writing in your voice (copytone)
tools.description: Writes in your own style from your samples: Claude learns your voice from your own writing and drafts outbound text (emails, posts) in it.

steps.title: Add writing samples for copytone (files, pasted text, or your own sent mail)
Check the voice
steps.text: In Claude Code, say: "test my copytone voice". Claude rewrites a short paragraph in your voice and asks if it sounds right.

tools.name: Task console
tools.description: A terminal-style window onto your main Claude Code session, with a Tasks page showing what each agent is doing.
tools.consent: Claude can update the Tasks page without asking each time. Hooks tell the console when each turn starts, ends (with Claude's last reply) or waits for you, and which model each session runs.

steps.title: Install
Install the web front end's packages
Build the web front end
Start the console server at every login, and add the console to the Start menu (a Windows scheduled task and a shortcut)
Claim your main session
steps.text:
Paste this into Claude Code (your main session, not a plain terminal):
  Run this with your Bash tool: uv run --project tools/console --frozen --no-sync console claim
The setup skill does this for you. Then open the console with:
  uv run --project tools/console --frozen --no-sync console open

tools.fix: Set the console up again with setup console.

tools.name: Voice and music control
tools.description: Speaks agents' notifications aloud in order, and plays, pauses and searches music (Spotify, or any app in the Windows media controls).
tools.consent: Claude can speak to you and control your music (play, pause, skip, queue, volume, liked songs, search, what's playing) without asking each time.

steps.title: Install (large: speech models and optional GPU libraries)
Create tools/audiohub/audiohub.toml and choose its settings (voice, ducking, wake phrases)
Spotify search, queue and volume (needs Spotify Premium)
steps.text:
1. Create a Web API app at https://developer.spotify.com/dashboard.
2. Register the redirect URI http://127.0.0.1:8888/callback exactly.
3. Copy the app's client ID (not secret) for the next step.

steps.title: Spotify client ID
Spotify sign-in (opens your browser)

tools.fix: Set the voice hub up again with setup audiohub.

tools.description: Lets Claude drive a dedicated Edge profile on sites you allow. Purchases, sends and deletes always wait for your OK.
tools.consent: Claude can drive the browser without asking each time. Purchases, sends and deletes still wait for your OK, unless you turned that off in its settings (for an action or a site).

steps.title: Install
Create tools/browser/browser.toml and choose its settings (allowed sites, downloads)

Auto-approve browser actions in Claude Code, so it doesn't ask before every click? The browser's own purchase, send and delete confirmations stay on either way, unless you turned them off in its settings.
Container browser (runs Edge in a throwaway Docker container; needs Docker Desktop, about 300 MB)
Copy the container browser's config

tools.fix: Set the browser up again with setup browser.

tools.name: Password vault
tools.description: Lets the browser log in to your accounts without any password reaching the model. Unlocks with Windows Hello.

steps.title: Install
Create the vault (Windows Hello asks three times)
Add logins
steps.text:
In your own terminal (never through Claude), add each login, for example:
  uv run --project tools/vault vault add github --name GitHub --origin https://github.com
It asks for the username and password itself.

tools.fix: Create the vault again with setup vault.

tools.consent: Claude can search, read and draft mail without asking each time. Sending still asks.

steps.text: Follow steps 1 to 3 of tools/mail/SETUP.md. They end with the client file saved at tools/mail/.state/google_client.json.

steps.title: Your Gmail address
Sign in (opens your browser)
More accounts

Add each extra account with its own alias, for example:

tools.description: Every morning, reads new mail, speaks what matters and emails you a short digest.
tools.consent: Its scheduled task runs Claude on its own every day at the times you chose (07:00 unless you changed it), locked down: it reads your mail by message id (whole threads included) and any file in life/, and edits your inbox, this week's plan and course READMEs there without asking; anything else is denied.

Run it every morning at 07:00 (a Windows scheduled task)

tools.description: Starts and drives headless Claude Code sessions in your other git repos, and lists past sessions to resume.
tools.consent: Claude can list your sessions and repos and check on a session without asking. Starting or messaging a session still asks.

steps.title: Install
Folders that hold your git repos (';'-separated, default C:\src)

tools.fix: Add it to Claude Code (setup wire, which also creates .env), or set background sessions up again with setup sessions.

tools.name: Projector whiteboard
tools.description: A projector and webcam turn a physical whiteboard into one Claude can see and draw on.
tools.consent: Claude can look at, draw on and clear the board, save, load and delete saved boards, switch its views (to-do list, tasks, idle, night sky), calibrate and realign it, and tick items in your weekly plan without asking each time.

steps.title: Install
Create tools/whiteboard/whiteboard.toml and choose its settings (projector, camera, morning run time)
List displays (set [display] name_match to your projector's name)
List cameras (set [camera] index if yours isn't 0)
Align the projector to the board
steps.text:
Point the webcam at the whole board, stand clear, then run:
  uv run --project tools/whiteboard whiteboard calibrate
or ask Claude to 'calibrate the board'.

steps.title: Morning keynotes and to-do list refresh at 06:00 (a Windows scheduled task; uses the optional life/ folder)

tools.fix: Check tools/whiteboard/whiteboard.toml, or set the whiteboard up again with setup whiteboard.

tools.name: Analysis chamber
tools.description: Takes a question, drafts a plan for you to check, then collects data, analyses it, has a fresh critic review the work and leaves a report and an agent for follow-up questions.
tools.consent: Claude can start an analysis, check on it, list runs and ask follow-up questions without asking each time. Each start or question runs its own Claude with permission checks off, which can run commands and read and write files on this PC to draft the plan or answer; its hooks try to block sends and, for a run you keep personal, writes into this repo. Approving a plan still asks.

steps.title: Install
Create tools/analysis-chamber/config.toml and choose its settings (where personal runs are kept, the one mailbox for signup mails)
Build the analysis kit (pandas, CUDA torch and more; slow the first time)
Start the chamber's daemon at every login (registers a Windows scheduled task; without it, runs start only after you start `analysis-chamber serve` yourself)

tools.fix: Check tools/analysis-chamber/config.toml, or set it up again with setup analysis-chamber.

tools.name: Sleep mode
tools.description: Darkens every screen and turns RGB lights off while the PC and agents keep running.
tools.consent: Claude can turn sleep mode on and off without asking each time.

steps.title: Install
Create tools/sleepmode/sleepmode.toml and choose its settings (RGB lighting)
RGB lights through OpenRGB
steps.text: Install OpenRGB (portable) at %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\OpenRGB\OpenRGB.exe and save your daytime look as an OpenRGB profile named 'day'. Without it, lights are left alone.

tools.fix: Set sleep mode up again with setup sleepmode.

tools.name: Job-application runner
tools.description: A scheduled headless Claude run that finds jobs matching your profile and applies through the browser tool, following your runbook.
tools.consent: Its scheduled task runs Claude on its own four times a day with every permission check off: it finds jobs and applies through its own browser profile (any site; it signs up and types passwords there, and only purchases and saved-login fills ask), and it can run commands and edit files without asking.

For resume tailoring (Windows only, needs Microsoft Word), also put the .docx it was made from there.
